proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2245 explains that ṭ/ṭh sitting stems were remade from upaviṣṭa, comparing Hindi baiṭhā/baiṭhnā and Gujarati bεṭho; addendum 14327 supplies the explicit upaviṣṭa node. The family is qualified because Turner notes contamination and phonetic difficulties, and some survey forms have reduced aspiration or added particles.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 4715 gives Prakrit calaï, Hindi calnā and Old Marwari calaï; contrast long-vowel cāl- under 4721. Each selected pair has two inflections of this same stem (cal-re includes a vocative particle); no gayo or other auxiliary is present. The survey’s vowel lengths and eastern e-vowels may not uniquely distinguish calati from calyati, and Turner documents contact spread into eastern languages.
